name: Amlodipine
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Amlodipine pharmacokinetics are not significantly affected by kidney impairment, so patients with kidney failure may receive the usual starting dose (US label). It is highly protein bound and not removed by hemodialysis.

bands.recommendation: Usual dosing: 5 mg once daily, maximum 10 mg (label).
Usual initial dose (label: patients with renal failure).

hd.text: No adjustment; hemodialysis is unlikely to remove amlodipine (label, Overdosage).

pd.text: No label adjustment; no PD data (amlodipine is hepatically cleared and not dialyzed).
pd.short: No label adjustment; no PD data

dialyzable: No: highly protein bound; hemodialysis not likely to help (label).
monitoring: Blood pressure, edema. Lower starting dose (2.5 mg) in older adults and hepatic impairment (label).

pediatric.approved_ages: Hypertension, 6 to 17 years; effect under 6 years unknown (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: 2.5 to 5 mg once daily (label gives fixed doses, not mg/kg).
pediatric.max_dose: 5 mg daily; higher doses not studied in children (label).

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney data; adult label needs no kidney adjustment.
No pediatric kidney data; adult label needs no kidney adjustment.
No pediatric kidney data; adult label needs no kidney adjustment.
No pediatric kidney data; adult label needs no kidney adjustment.

pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
